front_matter: World Bank Group and ID4D branding
Version 1.0 and date October 2019 prominently displayed
Abbreviations, acknowledgements, About this Guide, scope, organization, and references appear in front matter
The contents list includes separate indexes for tables, figures, and boxes
macrostructure: SECTION II. Designing an ID System
nested_structure_features: Section I includes 'Why ID matters for development' and 'ID 101: Basic concepts', with lower-level subtopics.
Section II combines principle-oriented guidance, a planning roadmap, key decisions, and procurement under one main section.
Section III groups topical modules such as legal framework and public engagement; these are thematic topics rather than a report's chronological execution log.
Front matter includes multiple navigation inventories (tables, figures, boxes, abbreviations, acknowledgements), indicating a long reference-guide use case.
The contents use typographic hierarchy and leader dots to connect heading names to page numbers; Roman-numeral front matter pagination transitions to numbered main-body pages.
visual_features: Cover uses dark navy, cyan, white and orange blocks, World Bank/ID4D logos, large lightweight uppercase title, and version/date emphasis.
Contents page has a large blue heading, bold major sections, increasingly indented lower levels, and dotted leaders aligned to right-side page numbers.
Back cover has a large solid navy field with the ID4D URL and institutional logos on a white footer strip.
This is a designed institutional guide rather than a standard academic paper; information architecture and navigation density support lookup and decision-making.
rights_caveats: World Bank attribution page states CC BY 3.0 IGO for the guide; third-party materials may have their own separate permission requirements.
No individual third-party charts or images were extracted or republished.
quality_and_generalization_notes: This source demonstrates a modular operational-guide architecture; it should not be used as a template for student reports or theses.
A guide organized for repeated consultation naturally uses detailed TOC structures and resource sections; those features are context-dependent.
